name: persuasion_c4
instructions: This is a charity-donation chat in which a persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate to Save the Children. Choose the persuasion strategy or dialogue act used by the LAST persuader message (the one marked 'Persuader message to tag'); use the earlier chat only to interpret it. Judge the function of the message in context, not just its topic.

criteria.greeting: Opening pleasantries: hello/hi, 'how are you', and small talk about how one's day is going (including answering such a question: 'I'm good, you?'). Usually early in the chat.
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Asks whether the other person knows/has heard of Save the Children or the organisation, or introduces the charity by asking about familiarity ('Have you heard of Save the Children?', 'Are you familiar with them?'). Early in the chat.
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Asks about the other person's own donation history, habits, involvement or opinions on charity in general ('Do you donate to charities?', 'Have you donated before?', 'What is your opinion about children's charity?').
criteria.task-related-inquiry: Asks a question about the task, the charity's work, or the person's thoughts/ideas on helping children or charity topics; also 'did you know...?' or 'what if I told you...' questions, and offers of more information ('Any questions?', 'Is there anything you want to know?').
criteria.proposition-of-donation: Directly invites or asks the person to donate (to Save the Children / from their task payment), e.g. 'Would you like to donate?', 'Would you consider donating?', 'Please do that', or explains the ask of donating part of the payment.
criteria.ask-donation-amount: A direct question asking how much/what amount or what share of the payment the person will donate ('How much would you like to donate?', 'What percentage of your payment?'). A plain yes/no invitation to donate is proposition-of-donation instead.
criteria.donation-information: Factual information about the donation itself: how it works in this task (deducted from the task payment, a box appears at the end, amounts allowed from $0 to $2, how donations are collected and sent), ways to give, and suggested or typical donation amounts or monthly figures stated as information.
criteria.credibility-appeal: Factual claims about Save the Children (or charities in general) that build trust or explain it: what it is, what it does, where it works, who runs it, ratings, transparency, finances, how funds are used, results and impact of the organisation, tax deductibility, and pointing to its website or URL to verify.
criteria.emotion-appeal: Appeals to feelings: suffering, need and hardship of children, statistics of children hurt/killed/starving, sad or heartbreaking imagery, 'children are our future', saving a child's life, feeling for the children, expressions of sympathy, guilt or sadness about their plight.
criteria.logical-appeal: Arguments or reasoning for why donating makes sense, without vivid emotional imagery: moral responsibility, cost-benefit reasoning, 'you get to feel good', 'if everyone gave a little it adds up', comparing alternatives, rebutting objections with reasons.
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Stresses that a small amount is enough: 'even $1 helps', 'every little bit counts', 'a few cents make a difference', 'you won't miss it'.
criteria.personal-story: Rare. The persuader recounts a first-person anecdote about their own life or experiences (their past, family, travels, feelings), told as a personal story. Stories about third parties, plain statements of where they work, and their own donations are not personal-story.
criteria.self-modeling: The persuader says they themselves donate or will donate (amounts, monthly donor, past giving) as a model for the other person.
criteria.praise-user: Compliments or praises the other person: 'you're so kind', 'that's great of you', 'people like you make the world better', admiration of their generosity or opinion.
criteria.thank: Expresses thanks or appreciation for the person's donation, help or time ('Thank you so much', 'much appreciated', 'the children will appreciate it').
criteria.acknowledgement: Short plain reaction showing agreement, understanding or receipt of what the other just said: 'sure', 'I agree', 'okay great', 'Yes they do', 'That's true', 'Great!' as a simple reply. Adds no persuasion, praise or thanks.
criteria.off-task: Rare. Chit-chat clearly unrelated to the charity and the task, e.g. small talk about the other person's home town, hobbies or pop culture. Polite goodbyes and 'have a great day' closings and questions about the other person's donating are NOT off-task.
criteria.other-closing: Polite goodbye, best wishes or a wrap-up of the chat ('have a great day', 'take care', 'we have chatted enough turns').
criteria.other-confirm: Confirming or clarifying a donation amount, payment method or payment details ('so you are donating $1, right?', 'how would you like to pay?', 'send me your PayPal').
criteria.other-hesitant-or-mirroring: A hesitant, grudging, bored or negative reaction ('Ok...', 'Fine...', 'Stupid'), or a mirroring reply ('Me too', 'Same here', 'I know what you mean') that just echoes the other person.
criteria.other-challenge-or-excuse: Pushback, excuses or complaints (the persuader says they are too busy or poor, challenges the other person's doubts or sources, says something negative about charities), not a persuasion attempt.
criteria.other-misc: Anything else that fits none of the named strategies: unclear fragments, answers to the other's question, remarks about other charities or the persuader's own volunteering, non-English text.
